content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes or bullish sentiment (especially when sentiment > 0.67); reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after strong bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.33) or prolonged downward trends; add 2–5% buffer to avoid premature bottoming.
- Lagging forecasts often overreact to recent sentiment shifts; adjust for 1–3 day delay in sentiment-driven price reactions.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to overfit recent volatility; apply smoothing or reduce volatility amplification.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Overshoot after bullish sentiment spikes: cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high if sentiment drops or stabilizes below 0.67.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extreme outliers (±15% from 14-day moving average) unless sentiment confirms breakout; use sentiment as filter for outlier rejection.
